issues.legal_issue: A broad arbitration clause in a principal agreement governs disputes under a related agreement when disputes under both agreements are referred and the agreements’ subject matters are integrally connected.
material_facts: The parties had principal agreements for the sale of flats and separate agreements for interior design work, each with its own arbitration clause.
The principal agreements’ arbitration clauses covered disputes connected with or arising in relation to their subject matter; the separate clauses named particular arbitrators.
The agreements overlapped in their specifications for fittings, finishes, and amenities, and the interior design work was to begin when those agreements were executed.
The claims before the arbitrator concerned disputes under both sets of agreements.
issues.conclusion: The general arbitration clause in the principal agreements governed the disputes under both sets of agreements, including the connected interior design disputes.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 16 and 34(2)(a)(iv) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitral tribunal may rule on its jurisdiction, and an award may be set aside if it decides matters outside the submission. The words “connected with, arising out of or in relation to” have wide scope and may include questions about the existence and effect of an arbitration agreement (Renusagar Power Co. Ltd. v. General Electric Co.). Where disputes under two agreements overlap and are connected, the broad clause in the principal agreement may govern disputes under both; a separate clause may operate where the disputes are confined to the separate agreement. The distinct, non-overlapping clauses in Aggarwal Engineering Co. v. T.H. Machine Industries illustrate the contrasting situation. The Court did not decide whether failure to raise a jurisdiction objection at the stage specified in section 16 precludes raising it later under section 34; it assumed the objection could be raised and decided the jurisdiction issue on its merits.

rule.if: award_set_aside_challenge and disputes_under_both_contracts and contracts_are_integrally_connected and main_clause_covers_connected_disputes

predicates.award_set_aside_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award in court seeking to have it set aside.
predicates.disputes_under_both_contracts: The claims referred to arbitration included disputes arising under both a principal contract and a separate related contract.
predicates.contracts_are_integrally_connected: The contracts concerned related work, their specifications overlapped, or performance under one was linked to performance under the other.
predicates.main_clause_covers_connected_disputes: The arbitration clause in the principal contract extended to disputes connected with or arising in relation to that contract’s subject matter.

issues.definition: When an award challenge concerns disputes under two integrally connected contracts and the principal contract’s arbitration clause covers connected disputes, that clause governs the joint disputes.

issues.legal_issue: A dispute seeking specific performance of a contract relating to immovable property may be referred to arbitration when the parties have agreed to arbitrate it.
material_facts: The awards directed specific performance of agreements for the sale of flats and related interior design agreements.
The dispute concerned contractual rights, and the parties’ agreements contained arbitration clauses.
No statutory prohibition applicable to the dispute was identified.
issues.conclusion: Disputes concerning specific performance of a contract may be referred to arbitration, so the subject matter was not incapable of arbitration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34(2)(b)(i) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, permits setting aside an award if the subject matter is not capable of settlement by arbitration. The Specific Relief Act, 1963, contains no prohibition on referring specific-performance disputes to arbitration, and the need to exercise discretion does not mean that only a court may exercise it. The Court approved Laxmi Narayan v. Raghubir Singh, Fertiliser Corporation of India v. Chemical Construction Corporation, and Keventer Agro Ltd. v. Seegram Comp. Ltd., and rejected the contrary view in PNB Finance Limited v. Shital Prasad Jain.

rule.if: award_set_aside_challenge and claim_seeks_specific_performance and parties_agreed_to_arbitrate and dispute_is_contractual_and_settleable

predicates.award_set_aside_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award in court seeking to have it set aside.
predicates.claim_seeks_specific_performance: The claim asks for an order requiring a party to perform a contract.
predicates.parties_agreed_to_arbitrate: The parties agreed to submit the dispute to arbitration.
predicates.dispute_is_contractual_and_settleable: The dispute concerns contractual rights that the parties may lawfully resolve by agreement.

issues.definition: A specific-performance claim concerning contractual rights is arbitrable when the parties agreed to arbitrate the dispute and it is lawfully settleable by agreement.

issues.legal_issue: A court considering an application to set aside an arbitral award cannot re-examine factual merits that do not fall within a statutory ground for setting aside.
material_facts: The challenge to the awards relied on factual disputes concerning default, whether time was essential, readiness and willingness, termination, and the merits of specific performance.
The Court found no issue showing that the subject matter was incapable of arbitration and no basis for treating the awards as conflicting with public policy.
The challenge did not establish another applicable statutory ground for setting aside the awards.
issues.conclusion: The factual merits raised did not provide a basis to set aside the awards under section 34(2)(b), and the Court rejected the challenge on those grounds.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, provides limited grounds for setting aside an award. Under section 34(2)(b), the relevant grounds are that the subject matter is not capable of arbitration or that the award conflicts with the public policy of India; the statutory explanation identifies fraud, corruption, and specified procedural violations as examples relevant to public policy. Disagreement with factual findings about contractual performance does not, by itself, establish one of those grounds.

rule.if: award_set_aside_challenge and challenge_targets_factual_merits and no_non_arbitrability_ground and no_public_policy_ground

predicates.award_set_aside_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award in court seeking to have it set aside.
predicates.challenge_targets_factual_merits: The challenge disputes factual findings about the parties’ performance, default, readiness, or contractual rights.
predicates.no_non_arbitrability_ground: The challenger has not established that the subject matter cannot lawfully be resolved by arbitration.
predicates.no_public_policy_ground: The challenger has not established that the award conflicts with public policy or otherwise identified a public-policy basis for setting it aside.

issues.definition: When an award challenge targets factual merits but establishes neither non-arbitrability nor a public-policy ground, the factual findings are not re-examined under the limited set-aside review.
